question: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) and Hepatitis E virus (HEV) are both transmitted by the faeco-oral route and are the most common causes of acute viral hepatitis in Indian children.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. HAV and HEV = faeco-oral transmission = most common causes of acute hepatitis in India. Hepatitis B, C, D = blood-borne (parenteral/perinatal). HAV is vaccine-preventable (not yet in National Immunization Schedule but recommended by IAP). HEV is dangerous in pregnancy — warn the family.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Both HAV and HEV are non-enveloped RNA viruses transmitted faeco-orally (contaminated water/food). HAV is the commonest cause of acute hepatitis in Indian children and is vaccine-preventable (2 doses, 12 months apart, from 12 months of age). HEV is notable for its high case-fatality rate in pregnancy (20–25%) due to acute liver failure. Neither causes chronic liver disease.
